claims.claim: Gandhi called off Non-Cooperation in February 1922 after a crowd set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura; 22 policemen died.
claims.quote: He abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement when in February 1922, a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station in Chauri Chaura. Twenty- two policemen were killed on that day.

claims.claim: The peasants at Chauri Chaura were provoked because police had fired on their peaceful demonstration.
claims.quote: The peasants were provoked because the police had fired on their peaceful demonstration.

claims.claim: Gandhi called the Chauri Chaura violence inhuman and called off the movement; Motilal Nehru, Jawaharlal Nehru, C.R. Das and Subhas Bose disapproved.
claims.quote: Viewing this as `inhuman conduct', Gandhi abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement, a decision which many in the Congress, including Motilal Nehru, Jawaharlal Nehru, Chittaranjan Das, and Subhas Chandra Bose disapproved of.

claims.claim: Gandhi felt the movement was turning violent and satyagrahis needed training.
claims.quote: He felt the movement was turning violent in many places and satyagrahis needed to be properly trained before they would be ready for mass struggles.

claims.claim: Some Congress leaders wanted to contest elections to the provincial councils set up under the 1919 Act, to oppose British policies from inside and show the councils were not truly democratic.
claims.quote: Within the Congress, some leaders were by now tired of mass struggles and wanted to participate in elections to the provincial councils that had been set up by the Government of India Act of 1919. They felt that it was important to oppose British policies within the councils, argue for reform and also demonstrate that these councils were not truly democratic.

claims.claim: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress to argue for a return to council politics.
claims.quote: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress to argue for a return to council politics.

claims.claim: Younger leaders Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Bose pressed for more radical mass agitation and full independence.
claims.quote: But younger leaders like Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose pressed for more radical mass agitation and for full independence.

claims.claim: After Non-Cooperation, Gandhians stressed constructive work in rural areas, while Das and Motilal Nehru wanted to fight council elections.
claims.quote: Gandhiji's followers stressed that the Congress must undertake constructive work in the rural areas. Other leaders such as Chitta Ranjan Das and Motilal Nehru argued that the party should fight elections to the councils and enter them in order to influence government policies.

claims.claim: Village social work in the mid-1920s extended the Gandhians' support base and helped launch the 1930 Civil Disobedience Movement.
claims.quote: Through sincere social work in villages in the mid-1920s, the Gandhians were able to extend their support base. This proved to be very useful in launching the Civil Disobedience movement in 1930.

claims.claim: The Swaraj Party tried a different strategy and was short-lived owing to Das's death in 1925.
claims.quote: Swaraj Party, which attempted a different strategy; owing to Das's death in 1925, it was short-lived.

claims.claim: C.R. Das was a lawyer from East Bengal, especially active in the Non-Cooperation Movement.
claims.quote: A major figure in the freedom movement, Das was a lawyer from East Bengal. He was especially active in the Non-Cooperation Movement.

claims.claim: Gandhi was released from prison in February 1924 and turned to khadi.
claims.quote: Mahatma Gandhi was released from prison in February 1924, and now chose to devote his attention to the promotion of home-spun cloth (khadi)

claims.claim: Gandhi was as much a social reformer as a politician; Indians had to rid themselves of child marriage and untouchability to be worthy of freedom.
claims.quote: For, Gandhiji was as much a social reformer as he was a politician. He believed that in order to be worthy of freedom, Indians had to get rid of social evils such as child marriage and untouchability.

claims.claim: Gandhi stressed khadi rather than imported mill cloth, for self-reliance.
claims.quote: Meanwhile, on the economic front Indians had to learn to become self-reliant – hence his stress on the significance of wearing khadi rather than mill-made cloth imported from overseas.

claims.claim: Gandhi stressed Hindu-Muslim harmony: Indians of one faith had to cultivate genuine tolerance for Indians of another.
claims.quote: Indians of one faith had also to cultivate a genuine tolerance for Indians of another – hence his emphasis on Hindu-Muslim harmony.

claims.claim: The charkha became the most abiding image of Indian nationalism.
claims.quote: Mahatma Gandhi with the charkha has become the most abiding image of Indian nationalism.

claims.claim: Gandhi saw the charkha as a symbol of a society that would not glorify machines; the spinning wheel could give the poor supplementary income and self-reliance.
claims.quote: He saw the charkha as a symbol of a human society that would not glorify machines and technology. The spinning wheel, moreover, could provide the poor with supplementary income and make them self-reliant.

claims.claim: For several years after Non-Cooperation Gandhi focused on social reform work.
claims.quote: For several years after the Non-cooperation Movement ended, Mahatma Gandhi focused on his social reform work.

claims.claim: The Simon Commission came to India in 1927 without a single Indian member; "Simon Go Back" slogans and black flags followed.
claims.quote: in 1927, the Simon Commission came to India to study constitutional reform, but without a single Indian member. Rallies and marches followed, with the slogan `Simon Go Back!' echoing through city streets and black flags being waved as a sign of resistance.

claims.claim: The Tory government set up a Statutory Commission under Sir John Simon to examine the constitutional system and suggest changes; it had no Indian member.
claims.quote: the new Tory government in Britain constituted a Statutory Commission under Sir John Simon. Set up in response to the nationalist movement, the commission was to look into the functioning of the constitutional system in India and suggest changes. The problem was that the commission did not have a single Indian member.

claims.claim: The Simon Commission arrived in 1928 and was greeted with "Go back Simon"; all parties, including Congress and the Muslim League, joined the demonstrations.
claims.quote: When the Simon Commission arrived in India in 1928, it was greeted with the slogan ‘Go back Simon’. All parties, including the Congress and the Muslim League, participated in the demonstrations.

claims.claim: In 1927 Britain decided to send a commission headed by Lord Simon with no Indian representative.
claims.quote: In 1927, the British government in England decided to send a commission headed by Lord Simon to decide India’s political future. The Commission had no Indian representative.

claims.claim: All political groups decided to boycott the Commission, which was met with banners saying Simon Go Back.
claims.quote: All political groups decided to boycott the Commission. When the Commission arrived, it was met with demonstrations with banners saying “Simon Go Back”.

claims.claim: The Simon Commission showed again the British refusal to consult Indians and strengthened calls for complete self-rule.
claims.quote: The Simon Commission laid bare once again the refusal of the British to genuinely consult Indians about their own future, strengthening calls for complete self-rule.

claims.claim: In Lahore in October 1928 Lala Lajpat Rai led a nonviolent march that police lathi-charged; badly injured, he addressed a meeting the same evening.
claims.quote: In Lahore in October 1928, Lala Lajpat Rai led a nonviolent march which the police brutally lathi-charged (i.e., attacked with sticks). Badly injured, he managed to address a meeting the same evening

claims.claim: Lajpat Rai, weakened by injuries, died two weeks later, which inflamed national sentiment.
claims.quote: Weakened by his injuries, Lala Lajpat Rai passed away two weeks later, which further inflamed national sentiment.

claims.claim: Lajpat Rai was assaulted by the police during a peaceful demonstration against the Simon Commission and died of his injuries.
claims.quote: Lala Lajpat Rai was assaulted by the British police during a peaceful demonstration against the Simon Commission. He succumbed to injuries that were inflicted on him during the demonstration.

claims.claim: In 1928 Gandhi began to think of re-entering politics; an all-India campaign opposed the all-White Simon Commission; he gave it his blessings but did not take part; same for the Bardoli peasant satyagraha.
claims.quote: In 1928, however, he began to think of re-entering politics. That year there was an all-India campaign in opposition to the all-White Simon Commission, sent from England to enquire into conditions in the colony. Gandhiji did not himself participate in this movement, although he gave it his blessings, as he also did to a peasant satyagraha in Bardoli in the same year.

claims.claim: Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli movement (1928) for peasant rights; Gandhi gave him the title Sardar.
claims.quote: Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli movement (1928) for peasant rights. It was one of the most successful grassroots movements in the freedom struggle. This led Mahatma Gandhi to bestow on him the title of ‘Sardar’.

claims.claim: HSRA was founded in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi; on 17 December 1928 Bhagat Singh, Azad and Rajguru killed Saunders, involved in the lathi-charge on Lajpat Rai.
claims.quote: they founded the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla in Delhi. On 17 December, 1928, Bhagat Singh, Azad and Rajguru assassinated Saunders, a police officer who was involved in the lathi-charge that had caused the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.

claims.claim: On 8 April 1929 Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly to "make the deaf hear".
claims.quote: On 8 April, 1929, Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly. The aim, as their leaflet explained, was not to kill but “to make the deaf hear”

claims.claim: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed on 23 March 1931.
claims.quote: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed on March 23, 1931.

claims.claim: In 1931 Suniti Chowdhury and Shanti Ghosh of Comilla killed a District Magistrate; Bina Das of Calcutta University tried to shoot the Governor of Bengal at a convocation.
claims.quote: In Comilla (in present-day Bangladesh), for example, Suniti Chowdhury and Shanti Ghosh, two students, assassinated a District Magistrate in 1931. A few months later, Bina Das, a student at Calcutta University, made a daring attempt on the life of the Governor of Bengal, during a convocation ceremony, but narrowly missed him

claims.claim: In 1928 a report drafted under Motilal Nehru called for Dominion status, with total internal autonomy.
claims.quote: In 1928, as a reaction to the Simon Commission, a report drafted under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru had called for India to be given `Dominion status' -- a status somewhat akin to the earlier `Home Rule', that is, with total internal autonomy;

claims.claim: Under dominion status Britain would still control the military and foreign policy and the British monarch would remain head of state.
claims.quote: Britain would still control India's military and foreign policy, and the British king or queen would still be the official head of state.

claims.claim: In 1927 Congress and the League tried to renegotiate an alliance; the main difference was representation in future assemblies.
claims.quote: The Congress and the Muslim League made efforts to renegotiate an alliance, and in 1927 it appeared that such a unity could be forged. The important differences were over the question of representation in the future assemblies that were to be elected.

claims.claim: Jinnah was willing to give up separate electorates if Muslims got reserved seats in the Central Assembly and population-proportionate representation in Bengal and Punjab.
claims.quote: Jinnah, one of the leaders of the Muslim League, was willing to give up the demand for separate electorates, if Muslims were assured reserved seats in the Central Assembly and representation in proportion to population in the Muslim-dominated provinces (Bengal and Punjab).

claims.claim: Hope of a settlement at the 1928 All Parties Conference vanished when M.R. Jayakar of the Hindu Mahasabha strongly opposed compromise.
claims.quote: Negotiations over the question of representation continued but all hope of resolving the issue at the All Parties Conference in 1928 disappeared when M.R. Jayakar of the Hindu Mahasabha strongly opposed efforts at compromise.

claims.claim: In October 1929 Viceroy Irwin offered a vague dominion status in an unspecified future and a Round Table Conference; Congress was not satisfied.
claims.quote: the viceroy, Lord Irwin, announced in October 1929, a vague offer of ‘dominion status’ for India in an unspecified future, and a Round Table Conference to discuss a future constitution. This did not satisfy the Congress leaders.

claims.claim: In December 1929, under Nehru's presidency, the Lahore Congress formalised Purna Swaraj; 26 January 1930 to be celebrated as Independence Day; the celebrations drew little attention, so Gandhi had to relate the abstract idea to everyday issues.
claims.quote: In December 1929, under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru, the Lahore Congress formalised the demand of ‘Purna Swaraj’ or full independence for India. It was declared that 26 January 1930, would be celebrated as the Independence Day when people were to take a pledge to struggle for complete independence. But the celebrations attracted very little attention. So Mahatma Gandhi had to find a way to relate this abstract idea of freedom to more concrete issues of everyday life.

claims.claim: The Purna Swaraj resolution was passed in December 1929 at the Lahore session.
claims.quote: The resolution demanding Purna Swaraj was passed in December 1929 at the Lahore session of the Congress.

claims.claim: Realising Britain was not ready to grant dominion status, younger leaders such as Nehru and Bose felt it was time for the more radical demand of Purna Swaraj.
claims.quote: Now, with growing popular anger and the realisation that Britain was not ready to grant India such a status, the younger Congress leaders, such as Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose, felt it was time for a more radical demand -- `Purna Swaraj' or complete independence.

claims.claim: Congress resolved for Purna Swaraj in 1929 under Jawaharlal Nehru; Independence Day observed 26 January 1930.
claims.quote: The decade closed with the Congress resolving to fight for Purna Swaraj (complete independence) in 1929 under the presidentship of Jawaharlal Nehru. Consequently, ‘Independence Day’ was observed on 26 January 1930 all over the country.

claims.claim: The Lahore session elected Nehru President, passing the baton to a younger generation, and proclaimed Purna Swaraj.
claims.quote: the election of Jawaharlal Nehru as President, signifying the passing of the baton of leadership to the younger generation; and the proclamation of commitment to “Purna Swaraj”, or complete independence.

claims.claim: The pledge: India must sever the British connection and attain Purna Swaraj or Complete Independence.
claims.quote: We believe, therefore, that India must sever the British connection and attain Purna Swaraj or Complete Independence.

claims.claim: The pledge said British rule had exploited the masses and ruined India economically, politically, culturally and spiritually.
claims.quote: The British Government in India has not only deprived the Indian people of their freedom but has based itself on the exploitation of the masses, and has ruined India economically, politically, culturally, and spiritually.

claims.claim: On 26 January 1930 Independence Day was observed with the national flag hoisted and patriotic songs sung.
claims.quote: On 26 January 1930, “Independence Day” was observed, with the national flag being hoisted in different venues, and patriotic songs being sung.

claims.claim: On 31 January 1930 Gandhi sent Irwin a letter with eleven demands, some general and some for specific classes.
claims.quote: On 31 January 1930, he sent a letter to Viceroy Irwin stating eleven demands. Some of these were of general interest; others were specific demands of different classes, from industrialists to peasants.

claims.claim: The demand to abolish the salt tax was the most stirring; salt is consumed by rich and poor alike.
claims.quote: The most stirring of all was the demand to abolish the salt tax. Salt was something consumed by the rich and the poor alike, and it was one of the most essential items of food.

claims.claim: Gandhi's letter was in a way an ultimatum: if demands were not met by 11 March the Congress would launch civil disobedience; Irwin was unwilling to negotiate.
claims.quote: Mahatma Gandhi’s letter was, in a way, an ultimatum. If the demands were not fulfilled by 11 March, the letter stated, the Congress would launch a civil disobedience campaign. Irwin was unwilling to negotiate.

claims.claim: Gandhi marched with 78 volunteers over 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi in 24 days.
claims.quote: So Mahatma Gandhi started his famous salt march accompanied by 78 of his trusted volunteers. The march was over 240 miles, from Gandhiji’s ashram in Sabarmati to the Gujarati coastal town of Dandi. The volunteers walked for 24 days, about 10 miles a day.

claims.claim: On 6 April Gandhi reached Dandi and ceremonially broke the salt law; this began the Civil Disobedience Movement.
claims.quote: On 6 April he reached Dandi, and ceremonially violated the law, manufacturing salt by boiling sea water. This marked the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

claims.claim: On 12 March 1930 Gandhi began walking from Sabarmati; he reached the sea three weeks later and made a fistful of salt.
claims.quote: On 12 March 1930, Gandhiji began walking from his ashram at Sabarmati towards the ocean. He reached his destination three weeks later, making a fistful of salt as he did and thereby making himself a criminal in the eyes of the law.

claims.claim: The Salt March of March-April 1930 was a 380-km march to Dandi, a coastal village in southern Gujarat.
claims.quote: It began with the Salt March in March-April 1930, when Gandhi led a 380-km march to Dandi, a coastal village in southern Gujarat

claims.claim: The state held a monopoly on salt and charged a high tax; breaking the salt law became a symbol.
claims.quote: Since the colonial government held a monopoly on salt production and charged a high tax for it, Gandhi saw the breaking of the colonial salt law as an appropriate symbol in the fight against colonial rule.

claims.claim: The Salt March tied the desire for freedom to a grievance shared by everybody.
claims.quote: The Salt March related the general desire of freedom to a specific grievance shared by everybody, and thus did not divide the rich and the poor.

claims.claim: Salt was indispensable in every household yet people could not make it even for domestic use.
claims.quote: For in every Indian household, salt was indispensable; yet people were forbidden from making salt even for domestic use, compelling them to buy it from shops at a high price.

claims.claim: The Civil Disobedience Movement asked people not only to refuse cooperation but also to break colonial laws (part 1).
claims.quote: How was this movement different from the Non-Cooperation Movement? People were now asked not only to refuse cooperation

claims.claim: ... with the British, as in 1921-22, but also to break colonial laws (part 2).
claims.quote: with the British, as they had done in 1921-22, but also to break colonial laws.

claims.claim: Thousands broke the salt law; foreign cloth was boycotted, liquor shops picketed, peasants refused revenue and chaukidari taxes, village officials resigned, forest people violated forest laws.
claims.quote: Thousands in different parts of the country broke the salt law, manufactured salt and demonstrated in front of government salt factories. As the movement spread, foreign cloth was boycotted, and liquor shops were picketed. Peasants refused to pay revenue and chaukidari taxes, village officials resigned, and in many places forest people violated forest laws

claims.claim: Thousands were arrested including Gandhi, but the movement spread with salt marches, boycott of foreign cloth and refusal to pay taxes.
claims.quote: Thousands were soon arrested, including Gandhi, but the Civil Disobedience Movement spread far and wide, with salt marches in other parts of the country, the boycott of foreign cloth, and the refusal to pay taxes.

claims.claim: Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a devout disciple of Gandhi, was arrested in April 1930; crowds in Peshawar faced armoured cars and police firing and many were killed.
claims.quote: When Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a devout disciple of Mahatma Gandhi, was arrested in April 1930, angry crowds demonstrated in the streets of Peshawar, facing armoured cars and police firing. Many were killed.

claims.claim: On 23 April 1930 at Qissa Khwani Bazaar in Peshawar British troops fired on a crowd peacefully protesting Abdul Ghaffar Khan's arrest.
claims.quote: Peshawar, a city of the North-West Frontier Province (in present-day northern Pakistan), witnessed the Qissa Khwani Bazaar massacre on April 23, 1930, when British troops fired on a crowd peacefully protesting the arrest of their leader, Abdul Ghaffar Khan, who was committed to nonviolent methods.

claims.claim: When Gandhi was arrested a month later, industrial workers in Sholapur attacked police posts, courts and railway stations.
claims.quote: A month later, when Mahatma Gandhi himself was arrested, industrial workers in Sholapur attacked police posts, municipal buildings, lawcourts and railway stations

claims.claim: The government used brutal repression: women and children were beaten and about 100,000 people were arrested.
claims.quote: A frightened government responded with a policy of brutal repression. Peaceful satyagrahis were attacked, women and children were beaten, and about 100,000 people were arrested.

claims.claim: After the Salt March nearly 60,000 Indians were arrested.
claims.quote: In the wake of the Salt March, nearly 60,000 Indians were arrested, among them, of course, Gandhiji himself.

claims.claim: Peasants breached forest laws, factory workers struck, lawyers boycotted courts and students left government schools.
claims.quote: Across large parts of India, peasants breached the hated colonial forest laws that kept them and their cattle out of the woods in which they had once roamed freely. In some towns, factory workers went on strike while lawyers boycotted British courts and students refused to attend government-run educational institutions.

claims.claim: Rich peasants (Patidars, Jats) joined because the trade depression hurt their commercial-crop income.
claims.quote: In the countryside, rich peasant communities – like the Patidars of Gujarat and the Jats of Uttar Pradesh – were active in the movement. Being producers of commercial crops, they were very hard hit by the trade depression and falling prices.

claims.claim: Rich peasants were disappointed when the movement was called off in 1931 without revenue revision; many refused to join when it restarted in 1932.
claims.quote: But they were deeply disappointed when the movement was called off in 1931 without the revenue rates being revised. So when the movement was restarted in 1932, many of them refused to participate.

claims.claim: Poorer tenants wanted unpaid rent remitted; the Congress was unwilling to support no-rent campaigns in most places.
claims.quote: Apprehensive of raising issues that might upset the rich peasants and landlords, the Congress was unwilling to support ‘no rent’ campaigns in most places.

claims.claim: Agricultural prices began to fall from 1926 and collapsed after 1930.
claims.quote: Agricultural prices began to fall from 1926 and collapsed after 1930.

claims.claim: Industrialists formed FICCI in 1927 (Purshottamdas Thakurdas, G.D. Birla) and supported the Civil Disobedience Movement at first.
claims.quote: To organise business interests, they formed the Indian Industrial and Commercial Congress in 1920 and the Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI) in 1927. Led by prominent industrialists like Purshottamdas Thakurdas and G.D. Birla, the industrialists attacked colonial control over the Indian economy, and supported the Civil Disobedience Movement when it was first launched.

claims.claim: After the failure of the Round Table Conference business groups were no longer uniformly enthusiastic: they feared militant activities, prolonged disruption and the growing influence of socialism.
claims.quote: But after the failure of the Round Table Conference, business groups were no longer uniformly enthusiastic. They were apprehensive of the spread of militant activities, and worried about prolonged disruption of business, as well as of the growing influence of socialism amongst the younger members of the Congress.

claims.claim: Industrial workers did not join in large numbers except in the Nagpur region.
claims.quote: The industrial working classes did not participate in the Civil Disobedience Movement in large numbers, except in the Nagpur region.

claims.claim: Railway workers struck in 1930 and dockworkers in 1932.
claims.quote: There were strikes by railway workers in 1930 and dockworkers in 1932.

claims.claim: The Congress was reluctant to include workers' demands, fearing it would alienate industrialists and divide anti-imperial forces.
claims.quote: But the Congress was reluctant to include workers’ demands as part of its programme of struggle. It felt that this would alienate industrialists and divide the anti-imperial forces.

claims.claim: During the salt march thousands of women came out of their homes to listen to Gandhi; they joined marches and made salt.
claims.quote: During Gandhiji’s salt march, thousands of women came out of their homes to listen to him. They participated in protest marches, manufactured salt, and

claims.claim: Gandhi held that women's duty was home and hearth; the Congress was long reluctant to give women positions of authority.
claims.quote: Gandhiji was convinced that it was the duty of women to look after home and hearth, be good mothers and good wives. And for a long time the Congress was reluctant to allow women to hold any position of authority within the organisation.

claims.claim: Large numbers of women broke the salt law, joined processions and picketed liquor and foreign-cloth shops.
claims.quote: Large numbers of women broke the salt law, took part in processions and in the picketing of liquor shops and shops selling foreign cloth.

claims.claim: Sarojini Naidu persuaded Gandhi to allow women into the Salt Satyagraha.
claims.quote: During the Salt Satyagraha, for instance, even Mahatma Gandhi was initially opposed to women’s participation. Sarojini Naidu had to persuade him to allow women to join the movement.

claims.claim: The Salt March was the first nationalist activity with large-scale women's participation; Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay persuaded Gandhi not to restrict protests to men.
claims.quote: Second, it was the first nationalist activity in which women participated in large numbers. The socialist activist Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay had persuaded Gandhiji not to restrict the protests to men alone.

claims.claim: Sarojini Naidu was a leader of the Dandi March and the first Indian woman President of the Congress (1925).
claims.quote: Naidu was a significant leader of the Dandi March. She was the first Indian woman to become President of the Indian National Congress (1925).

claims.claim: The Salt March first brought Gandhi to world attention.
claims.quote: First, it was this event that first brought Mahatma Gandhi to world attention.

claims.claim: The Salt March made the British realise that they would have to devolve some power to Indians.
claims.quote: Third, and perhaps most significant, it was the Salt March which forced upon the British the realisation that their Raj would not last forever, and that they would have to devolve some power to the Indians.

claims.claim: In 1931 Irwin agreed with Gandhi to release non-violent political prisoners and allow limited private salt-making; Congress suspended civil disobedience and agreed to attend the Round Table Conference. First formal negotiation between Britain and Congress as equals.
claims.quote: in 1931, Viceroy Irwin made an agreement with Gandhi: the government released political prisoners who had not been involved in violence and allowed a limited private manufacture of salt. In return, the Congress suspended civil disobedience and agreed to participate in a Round Table Conference in London. The pact marked the first formal negotiation between the British government and the Congress as equals, but the Round Table Conference failed to produce a breakthrough.

claims.claim: Gandhi called off the movement and made a pact with Irwin on 5 March 1931.
claims.quote: In such a situation, Mahatma Gandhi once again decided to call off the movement and entered into a pact with Irwin on 5 March 1931.

claims.claim: Gandhi agreed to attend a Round Table Conference in London and the government agreed to release political prisoners; in December 1931 he went but negotiations broke down.
claims.quote: Round Table Conference) in London and the government agreed to release the political prisoners. In December 1931, Gandhiji went to London for the conference, but the negotiations broke down and he returned disappointed.

claims.claim: To that end the British convened Round Table Conferences; the first met in November 1930 without Gandhi; Gandhi was released in January 1931 and met the Viceroy in February; the Gandhi-Irwin Pact ended civil disobedience, freed prisoners and allowed salt manufacture along the coast.
claims.quote: To that end, the British government convened a series of “Round Table Conferences” in London. The first meeting was held in November 1930, but without the pre-eminent political leader in India, thus rendering it an exercise in futility. Gandhiji was released from jail in January 1931 and the following month had several long meetings with the Viceroy. These culminated in what was called the “Gandhi-Irwin Pact’, by the terms of which civil disobedience would be called off, all prisoners released, and salt manufacture allowed along the coast.

claims.claim: Radical nationalists criticised the pact because Gandhi got no commitment to independence, only an assurance of talks.
claims.quote: The pact was criticised by radical nationalists, for Gandhiji was unable to obtain from the Viceroy a commitment to political independence for Indians; he could obtain merely an assurance of talks towards that possible end.

claims.claim: Younger Congress leaders criticised the pact because it did not guarantee Purna Swaraj.
claims.quote: The pact was criticised by younger Congress leaders as it did not guarantee Purna Swaraj.

claims.claim: At the second Round Table Conference Gandhi represented the Congress; his claim to speak for all India was challenged by the Muslim League, the Princes and Ambedkar.
claims.quote: A second Round Table Conference was held in London in the latter part of 1931. Here, Gandhiji represented the Congress. However, his claims that his party represented all of India came under challenge from three parties: from the Muslim League, which claimed to stand for the interests of the Muslim minority; from the Princes, who claimed that the Congress had no stake in their territories; and from the brilliant lawyer and thinker B.R. Ambedkar, who argued that Gandhiji and the Congress did not really represent the lowest castes.

claims.claim: The London conference was inconclusive; Gandhi resumed civil disobedience under the new Viceroy Lord Willingdon.
claims.quote: The Conference in London was inconclusive, so Gandhiji returned to India and resumed civil disobedience. The new Viceroy, Lord Willingdon, was deeply unsympathetic to the Indian leader.

claims.claim: On return Gandhi found a new round of repression: Ghaffar Khan and Nehru in jail, Congress declared illegal; he relaunched civil disobedience and by 1934 it lost momentum.
claims.quote: Back in India, he discovered that the government had begun a new cycle of repression. Ghaffar Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru were both in jail, the Congress had been declared illegal, and a series of measures had been imposed to prevent meetings, demonstrations and boycotts. With great apprehension, Mahatma Gandhi relaunched the Civil Disobedience Movement. For over a year, the movement continued, but by 1934 it lost its momentum.

claims.claim: Gandhi tried to resume civil disobedience but massive arrests followed and enthusiasm was missing; he withdrew the movement in 1934.
claims.quote: Gandhi tried to resume the Civil Disobedience Movement, but the British responded with massive arrests, and public enthusiasm was now missing. Gandhi withdrew the movement in 1934, after

claims.claim: March 1931 Gandhi ends CDM; December 1931 second Round Table Conference; 1932 civil disobedience re-launched.
claims.quote: March 1931 Gandhiji ends Civil Disobedience Movement. December 1931 Second Round Table Conference. 1932 Civil Disobedience re-launched.

claims.claim: Ambedkar organised the Depressed Classes Association in 1930, demanded separate electorates at the second Round Table Conference; Gandhi fasted unto death; Poona Pact of September 1932 gave reserved seats voted by the general electorate.
claims.quote: Dr B.R. Ambedkar, who organised the dalits into the Depressed Classes Association in 1930, clashed with Mahatma Gandhi at the second Round Table Conference by demanding separate electorates for dalits. When the British government conceded Ambedkar’s demand, Gandhiji began a fast unto death. He believed that separate electorates for dalits would slow down the process of their integration into society. Ambedkar ultimately accepted Gandhiji’s position and the result was the Poona Pact of September 1932. It gave the Depressed Classes (later to be known as the Schedule Castes) reserved seats in provincial and central legislative councils, but they were to be voted in by the general electorate.

claims.claim: Ambedkar thought separate electorates the only way to ensure political voice; Gandhi feared they would divide Hindu society and fasted; the Poona Pact increased reserved seats instead.
claims.quote: he believed that keeping separate electorates for the Depressed Classes was the only way to ensure their political voice. Gandhi, on the other hand, feared this would permanently divide Hindu society and began a `fast unto death' in protest. A compromise was reached in the so-called `Poona Pact', which, instead of separate electorates, increased the number of reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in the legislatures.

claims.claim: During the movement's later phase Gandhi focused more on social reform, specifically the campaign against untouchability, the discrimination suffered by those rejected by the caste system.
claims.quote: During that time, Gandhi focused more on social reforms, specifically his campaign against untouchability, i.e. the discrimination suffered by those rejected by the caste system

claims.claim: Gandhi declared swaraj would not come for a hundred years if untouchability was not eliminated and called untouchables harijan.
claims.quote: But Mahatma Gandhi declared that swaraj would not come for a hundred years if untouchability was not eliminated. He called the ‘untouchables’ harijan,

claims.claim: Gandhi organised satyagraha for temple entry and access to wells, tanks, roads and schools.
claims.quote: or the children of God, organised satyagraha to secure them entry into temples, and access to public wells, tanks, roads and schools.

claims.claim: Gandhi opposed separate electorates for the lower castes, believing it would prevent integration and permanently segregate them.
claims.quote: Mahatma Gandhi opposed the demand for separate electorates for “lower castes”. He believed that this would prevent their integration into mainstream society and permanently segregate them from other caste Hindus.

claims.claim: The dalit movement stayed apprehensive of the Congress-led national movement.
claims.quote: The dalit movement, however, continued to be apprehensive of the Congress-led national movement.

claims.claim: Muslims generally kept away from the Civil Disobedience Movement.
claims.quote: Muslims generally kept away from the Civil Disobedience Movement.

claims.claim: In 1930 Iqbal presided over the Muslim League session at Allahabad and proposed a separate territory for Muslims in the north-west within a larger Indian federation; not yet the precise idea of Pakistan.
claims.quote: When Muhammad Iqbal, a philosopher and poet of Urdu, presided over the 1930 All-India Muslim League session in Allahabad (present-day Prayagraj), he proposed a separate territory for Muslims in northwestern India, which would enable Muslims to preserve their culture and religious identity within a larger Indian federation. While this was not yet the precise idea of Pakistan (the word was coined a few years later), this intensified the debate about separateness.

claims.claim: In 1930 Iqbal, as League president, stressed separate electorates; his statement is supposed to have given intellectual justification for the later Pakistan demand.
claims.quote: In 1930, Sir Muhammad Iqbal, as president of the Muslim League, reiterated the importance of separate electorates for the Muslims as an important safeguard for their minority political interests. His statement is supposed to have provided the intellectual justification for the Pakistan demand that came up in subsequent years.

claims.claim: Some Muslim political organisations were lukewarm to the movement; many Muslims felt alienated after the decline of Non-Cooperation-Khilafat.
claims.quote: Some of the Muslim political organisations in India were also lukewarm in their response to the Civil Disobedience Movement. After the decline of the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement, a large section of Muslims felt alienated from the Congress.

claims.claim: In 1935 Britain conceded some provincial autonomy: elected provincial governments, but foreign affairs, defence and internal security stayed with the British; governors could take over provincial administration.
claims.quote: In 1935, the British conceded some degree of provincial autonomy. The reform allowed for elected governments at the provincial level, although the colonial powers retained much control, including foreign affairs, defence, and internal security. The British-appointed governors could also indefinitely take over provincial administration.

claims.claim: The 1935 Act prescribed provincial autonomy; elections announced for 1937; Congress formed governments in 7 of 11 provinces.
claims.quote: The combined struggles of the Indian people bore fruit when the Government of India Act of 1935 prescribed provincial autonomy and the government announced elections to the provincial legislatures in 1937. The Congress formed governments in 7 out of 11 provinces.

claims.claim: In 1935 a new Act promised some representative government; two years later, with a restricted franchise, Congress won; eight of 11 provinces had Congress ministries under a British Governor.
claims.quote: In 1935, however, a new Government of India Act promised some form of representative government. Two years later, in an election held on the basis of a restricted franchise, the Congress won a comprehensive victory. Now eight out of 11 provinces had a Congress “Prime Minister”, working under the supervision of a British Governor.

claims.claim: Under the 1935 Act the executive became almost entirely responsible to provincial legislatures; in the 1937 elections Congress came to power in eight of 11 provinces.
claims.quote: The executive was made partly responsible to the provincial legislature in 1919, and almost entirely so under the Government of India Act of 1935. When elections were held in 1937, under the 1935 Act, the Congress came to power in eight out of the 11 provinces.

claims.claim: Even in 1935 the electorate was no more than 10 to 15 per cent of adults; legislatures worked under colonial rule and were responsible to the British-appointed Governor.
claims.quote: even in 1935 it remained limited to no more than 10 to 15 per cent of the adult population: there was no universal adult franchise. The legislatures elected under the 1935 Act operated within the framework of colonial rule, and were responsible to the Governor appointed by the British.

claims.claim: Provincial autonomy means the capacity of provinces to make relatively independent decisions while remaining in a federation.
claims.quote: Provincial autonomy Capacity of the provinces to make relatively independent decisions while remaining within a federation

claims.claim: The 1937 elections convinced the League that Muslims were a minority; Congress refused a joint Congress-League government in the United Provinces in 1937.
claims.quote: the provincial elections of 1937 seemed to have convinced the League that Muslims were a minority, and they would always have to play second fiddle in any democratic structure. It feared that Muslims may even go unrepresented. The Congress’s rejection of the League’s desire to form a joint Congress-League government in the United Provinces in 1937 also annoyed the League.

claims.claim: In September 1939, after two years of Congress rule, the Second World War began; Congress offered support in return for independence after the war; the British refused and the Congress ministries resigned.
claims.quote: In September 1939, after two years of Congress rule in the provinces, the Second World War broke out. Critical of Hitler, Congress leaders were ready to support the British war effort. But in return they wanted that India be granted independence after the war. The British refused to concede the demand. The Congress ministries resigned in protest.

claims.claim: 1935 Government of India Act; 1939 Congress ministries resign.
claims.quote: 1935 Government of India Act promises some form of representative government

claims.claim: In the 1938 Haripura Congress session Gandhi and Subhas were photographed in cheerful conversation, though they differed on many issues; the next year Subhas resigned the Congress presidency.
claims.quote: নীচের ছবিটা ১৯৩৮ খ্রিস্টাব্দের হরিপুরা কংগ্রেস অধিবেশনের সময় তোলা একটি ফটোগ্রাফ। ছবিতে গান্ধি ও সুভাষ হাস্যমুখর আলাপে ব্যস্ত। অথচ ঐ সময়ে নানা প্রসঙ্গে দু-জনের মধ্যে মতবিরোধ ছিল। এমনকি পরের বছর সুভাষচন্দ্র কংগ্রেস-সভাপতির পদ ত্যাগ করেছিলেন।

claims.claim: Bose was a radical nationalist with socialist leanings who did not share Gandhi's ideal of ahimsa.
claims.quote: A radical nationalist, with socialist leanings, Bose did not share Gandhiji’s ideal of ahimsa

claims.claim: Bose broke from Gandhi's non-violence, convinced freedom would come only through armed struggle.
claims.quote: Subhas Chandra Bose, once a Congress leader, broke away from Gandhi’s policies of nonviolence, convinced that freedom would come only through armed struggle.

claims.claim: In January 1941 Bose secretly left his Calcutta home and later raised the Azad Hind Fauj (INA).
claims.quote: In January 1941, he secretly left his Calcutta home, went to Singapore, via Germany, and raised the Azad Hind Fauj or the Indian National Army (INA).

claims.claim: Non-Cooperation began with Gandhi promising Swaraj within a year if people adhered strictly to nonviolence.
claims.quote: thus began the Non-Cooperation Movement, with Gandhi promising Swaraj within a year if people adhered strictly to nonviolence.

claims.claim: In 1920 an alliance was forged between Khilafat leaders and the Congress to fight together for Khilafat and Swaraj.
claims.quote: In 1920, an alliance was forged between Khilafat leaders and the Congress, with Gandhi and Khilafat leaders promising to fight together for both Khilafat and Swaraj.

claims.claim: Dalit leaders demanded reserved seats in educational institutions and a separate electorate to choose dalit members for legislative councils.
claims.quote: demanding reserved seats in educational institutions, and a separate electorate that would choose dalit members for legislative councils.

claims.claim: The HRA reorganised itself as the HSRA; its leaders Chandrashekar Azad and Bhagat Singh wanted to avenge Lajpat Rai.
claims.quote: The HRA reorganised itself as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). Its leaders, Chandrashekar Azad and Bhagat Singh, were keen to avenge Lala Lajpat Rai's death.

claims.claim: Many freedom fighters disagreed with Gandhi's slow non-violent path and thought force legitimate.
claims.quote: In disagreement with Gandhi's path of non-violence and its slow pace that was seen as not putting sufficient pressure on the colonial rulers, many freedom fighters believed that the use of force was a legitimate means to achieve independence.

claims.claim: Bina Das said in her confession she wanted to free her country from perpetual subjection; she was sentenced to nine years of rigorous imprisonment.
claims.quote: stated in her confession that she wanted to free her country from the "perpetual subjection to infinite shame and endless suffering" caused by the British occupation. (She was sentenced to nine years of rigorous imprisonment.)

claims.claim: When the Civil Disobedience Movement started there was an atmosphere of suspicion and distrust between communities.
claims.quote: When the Civil Disobedience Movement started there was thus an atmosphere of suspicion and distrust between communities.

claims.claim: Radicals led by Nehru and Bose became more assertive; liberals and moderates lost influence.
claims.quote: Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose, became more assertive. The liberals and moderates, who were proposing a constitutional system within the framework of British dominion, gradually lost their influence.

claims.claim: The demand for complete independence was not new: the nationalist faction of the Congress had voiced it two decades earlier and Aurobindo in 1908.
claims.quote: This was not a completely new demand. Nationalist faction of the Congress had voiced it two decades earlier, and Aurobindo had raised a similar demand in 1908.

claims.claim: The pledge declared it the inalienable right of the Indian people to freedom and the right to alter or abolish an oppressive government.
claims.quote: We believe that it is the inalienable right of the Indian people, as of any other people, to have freedom and to enjoy the fruits of their toil and have the necessities of life, so that they may have full opportunities of growth. We believe also that if any government deprives a people of these rights and oppresses them, the people have a further right to alter it or to abolish it.

claims.claim: Though Gandhi gave Irwin advance notice of the Salt March, Irwin failed to grasp its significance.
claims.quote: Although Gandhiji had given advance notice of his “Salt March” to the Viceroy Lord Irwin, Irwin failed to grasp the significance of the action.

claims.claim: Parallel salt marches were conducted in other parts of the country.
claims.quote: Meanwhile, parallel salt marches were being conducted in other parts of the country.

claims.claim: Thousands came to hear Gandhi wherever he stopped; he explained what he meant by swaraj and urged peaceful defiance.
claims.quote: Thousands came to hear Mahatma Gandhi wherever he stopped, and he told them what he meant by swaraj and urged them to peacefully defy the British.

claims.claim: During the First World War Indian merchants and industrialists made huge profits and became powerful; they now reacted against colonial policies that restricted business.
claims.quote: During the First World War, Indian merchants and industrialists had made huge profits and become powerful (see Chapter 5). Keen on expanding their business, they now reacted against colonial policies that restricted business activities.

claims.claim: Some workers selectively adopted Gandhian ideas such as boycott of foreign goods in their own movements against low wages and poor conditions.
claims.quote: But in spite of that, some workers did participate in the Civil Disobedience Movement, selectively adopting some of the ideas of the Gandhian programme, like boycott of foreign goods, as part of their own movements against low wages and poor working conditions.

claims.claim: In 1930 thousands of Chotanagpur tin-mine workers wore Gandhi caps and joined rallies and boycotts.
claims.quote: In 1930 thousands of workers in Chotanagpur tin mines wore Gandhi caps and participated in protest rallies and boycott campaigns.

claims.claim: Women picketed foreign cloth and liquor shops and many went to jail.
claims.quote: picketed foreign cloth and liquor shops. Many went to jail.

claims.claim: A British report noted that thousands of women, many of good family and high education, emerged from the seclusion of their homes, even from purdah, to join Congress demonstrations.
claims.quote: A British report noted that `thousands of women, many being of good family and high educational attainments, suddenly emerged from the seclusion of their homes, and, in some instances, actually from purdah (screen, veil), in order to join Congress demonstrations

claims.claim: After 1934 the Congress turned to constitutional methods, seeking substantial concessions through negotiations.
claims.quote: which the Congress turned to constitutional methods, seeking substantial concessions through complex negotiations.

claims.claim: The Depressed Classes is the official terminology; the Constitution calls them Scheduled Castes.
claims.quote: earlier called `Untouchables' or, in the official terminology, `Depressed Classes'; the Indian Constitution refers to them as `Scheduled Castes'.

claims.claim: From around the 1930s the untouchables began to call themselves dalit; for long the Congress had ignored them for fear of offending the sanatanis.
claims.quote: One such group was the nation’s ‘untouchables’, who from around the 1930s had begun to call themselves dalit or oppressed. For long the Congress had ignored the dalits, for fear of offending the sanatanis, the conservative high-caste Hindus.

claims.claim: Dalit leaders believed political empowerment would resolve their social disabilities.
claims.quote: Political empowerment, they believed, would resolve the problems of their social disabilities.

claims.claim: Many Muslim leaders feared that minority culture and identity would be submerged under Hindu majority domination.
claims.quote: Many Muslim leaders and intellectuals expressed their concern about the status of Muslims as a minority within India. They feared that the culture and identity of minorities would be submerged under the domination of a Hindu majority.

claims.claim: As Hindu-Muslim relations worsened, religious processions with militant fervour provoked communal clashes and riots in various cities.
claims.quote: As relations between Hindus and Muslims worsened, each community organised religious processions with militant fervour, provoking Hindu-Muslim communal clashes and riots in various cities.

claims.claim: Gandhi argued at the Round Table Conference that separate electorates would ensure bondage in perpetuity for the untouchables.
claims.quote: Separate electorates to the “Untouchables” will ensure them bondage in perpetuity

claims.claim: Ambedkar wrote that the depressed classes were economically dependent on high-caste Hindus.
claims.quote: Economically, it is a class entirely dependent upon the high-caste Hindus for earning its daily bread with no independent way of living open to it.

claims.claim: Ambedkar held that some share of political power was a paramount necessity for the Depressed Classes to protect themselves.
claims.quote: some share of political power in order that it may protect itself is a paramount necessity

claims.claim: The Acts of 1909, 1919 and 1935 were not directly debated and formulated by Indians; they were enacted by the colonial government.
claims.quote: the Acts (1909, 1919 and 1935) were not directly debated and formulated by Indians. They were enacted by the colonial government.

claims.claim: Earlier constitutional developments should not be seen as an unbroken continuity with the events after 1946.
claims.quote: Yet we should not see an unbroken continuity between the earlier constitutional developments and what happened in the three years from 1946.

claims.claim: Gandhi and his followers marched over 240 miles from Sabarmati to the coastal town of Dandi and broke the law by gathering natural salt and boiling sea water.
claims.quote: Gandhiji and his followers marched for over 240 miles from Sabarmati to the coastal town of Dandi where they broke the government law by gathering natural salt found on the seashore, and boiling sea water to produce salt.

claims.claim: Jinnah reorganised the Muslim League after 1934.
claims.quote: He reorganised the Muslim League after 1934, and became the major spokesperson for the demand for Pakistan.

claims.claim: WBBSE: Chauri Chaura was a village in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh; on 4 February 1922 local people gathered to protest.
claims.quote: হিংসার চূড়ান্ত প্রকাশ ঘটেছিল উত্তর প্রদেশের গোরক্ষপুর জেলার চৌরিচৌরা গ্রামে। ১৯২২ খ্রিস্টাব্দের ৪ ফেব্রুয়ারি ঐ গ্রামের স্থানীয় মানুষেরা প্রতিবাদ জানাতে সমবেত হন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: police chased by the crowd entered the station, the door was shut from outside and it was set on fire; Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement.
claims.quote: জনতার তাড়ায় পুলিশেরা থানায় ঢুকে পড়লে থানার দরজা বন্ধ করে বাইরে থেকে আগুন লাগিয়ে দেওয়া হয়। এই ঘটনায় গান্ধি অহিংস অসহযোগ আন্দোলন তুলে নিয়েছিলেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: many Congress leaders criticised Gandhi for this decision.
claims.quote: তবে জাতীয় কংগ্রেসের অনেক নেতাই এই সিদ্ধান্তের জন্য গান্ধির সমালোচনা করেছিলেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: Das, Motilal Nehru and others said the Congress should leave Gandhi's path and take part in the government legislative councils rather than boycott them.
claims.quote: কংগ্রেসের মধ্যে চিত্তরঞ্জন দাশ ও মোতিলাল নেহরু প্রমুখ নেতারা গান্ধির পন্থা থেকে বেরিয়ে আসার কথা বলেছিলেন। তাঁদের মতে সরকারি আইন পরিষদকে বয়কট না করে তাতে অংশ নেওয়া উচিত।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in the later part of 1922 Das and Motilal Nehru together formed the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party, which worked as a group within the Congress.
claims.quote: ফলে ১৯২২ খ্রিস্টাব্দের শেষে দিকে চিত্তরঞ্জন দাশ ও মোতিলাল নেহরু মিলে কংগ্রেস-খিলাফৎ স্বরাজ্য দল তৈরি করেন। ঐ দলটি কংগ্রেসের মধ্যেই একটি গোষ্ঠী হিসেবে কাজ করতে থাকে।

claims.claim: WBBSE: after Das died (1925) the groups became one.
claims.quote: চিত্তরঞ্জন দাশ মারা যাওয়ার পর (১৯২৫ খ্রিস্টাব্দ) গোষ্ঠীগুলি এক হয়ে যায়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: the Swaraj Party won the 1924 Calcutta Corporation election; Das became Mayor; Subhas became Chief Executive Officer; Subhas was the party's secretary and a director of the Forward newspaper.
claims.quote: চিত্তরঞ্জন ও মোতিলাল নেহরুর স্বরাজ্য দলের সচিব ছিলেন সুভাষচন্দ্র। স্বরাজ্য দলের তরফে ফরওয়ার্ড পত্রিকার অন্যতম পরিচালকের দায়িত্ব নেন সুভাষ। ১৯২৪ খ্রিস্টাব্দে কলকাতা কর্পোরেশনের নির্বাচনে স্বরাজ্য দল জিতে যায়। চিত্তরঞ্জন কর্পোরেশনের মেয়র হন। সুভাষচন্দ্র প্রধান কার্যনির্বাহকের দায়িত্ব পান।

claims.claim: WBBSE: after Das died in 1925 Subhas began on his own initiative to propound Purna Swaraj.
claims.quote: ১৯২৫ খ্রিস্টাব্দে চিত্তরঞ্জন দাশের মৃত্যু হয়। তখন থেকেই সুভাষচন্দ্র নিজের উদ্যোগে পূর্ণ স্বরাজের পক্ষে বক্তব্য প্রচার করতে থাকেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: the conflict between Subhas and Gandhi began at the 1928 Calcutta session.
claims.quote: বিষয়কে কেন্দ্র করে ১৯২৮ খ্রিস্টাব্দে কলকাতা অধিবেশনে গান্ধির সঙ্গে সুভাষের সংঘাত শুরু হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: Subhas was not fully committed to Gandhi's ideal of non-violence.
claims.quote: সুভাষচন্দ্র গান্ধির অহিংসার আদর্শে পুরোপুরি বিশ্বাসী না হলেও

claims.claim: WBBSE: in November 1927 the colonial government created a commission under Sir John Simon to examine Indians' constitutional rights, with no Indian member; all Indian political organisations opposed it.
claims.quote: ১৯২৭ খ্রিস্টাব্দের নভেম্বর মাসে ঔপনিবেশিক সরকার ভারতীয়দের সাংবিধানিক অধিকার খতিয়ে দেখার জন্য একটি কমিশন তৈরি করে। স্যর জন সাইমনের নেতৃত্বে ঐ কমিশনে কোনো ভারতীয় সদস্য ছিল না। ফলে ভারতের সমস্ত রাজনৈতিক সংগঠনগুলি সাইমন কমিশনের বিরোধিতা করে।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in hartals all over the country the commission was shown black flags and the cry "Simon go back" was raised.
claims.quote: দেশজোড়া বিভিন্ন হরতালে কমিশনকে কালো পতাকা দেখিয়ে আওয়াজ তোলা হয়েছিল ‘সাইমন ফিরে যাও’।

claims.claim: WBBSE: as a result of the anti-Simon efforts the Congress under Gandhi's leadership declared Purna Swaraj in 1929.
claims.quote: সাইমন কমিশন-বিরোধী উদ্যোগগুলির ফলে ১৯২৯ খ্রিস্টাব্দে গান্ধির নেতৃত্বে কংগ্রেস পূর্ণস্বরাজ অর্জনের কথা ঘোষণা করে।

claims.claim: WBBSE: on 6 April 1930 Gandhi marched to Dandi in Gujarat and broke the salt law, symbolically rejecting colonial rule with a fistful of salt.
claims.quote: ১৯৩০ খ্রিস্টাব্দের ৬ এপ্রিল গুজরাটের ডান্ডিতে অভিযান করে লবণ আইন ভঙ্গ করেন গান্ধি। সমুদ্রের তটভূমি থেকে একমুঠো লবণ তুলে গান্ধি প্রতীকীভাবে ভারতবর্ষে ঔপনিবেশিক শাসনকে অস্বীকার করেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: stopping tax payment and boycott of foreign goods began; the government confiscated the land of peasants who refused revenue; women joined in large numbers.
claims.quote: সরকারকে কর দেওয়া বন্ধ করার পাশাপাশি বিদেশি দ্রব্য বয়কট করা শুরু হয়। কৃষকরা রাজস্ব দিতে অস্বীকার করায় তাদের জমি বাজেয়াপ্ত করে নেয় সরকার। ব্যাপক সংখ্যায় নারীরা আইন অমান্য আন্দোলনে যোগ দিয়েছিলেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in the north-west under Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan the Pathans joined Civil Disobedience as non-violent Gandhians.
claims.quote: ভারতের উত্তর-পশ্চিম প্রান্তে খান আবদুল গফফর খানের নেতৃত্বে পাঠানরা আইন অমান্য আন্দোলনে শামিল হয়েছিলেন। তাঁরা ছিলেন অহিংস গান্ধিবাদী সংগ্রামী।

claims.claim: WBBSE: the organisation was Khudai Khidmatgar (Red Shirts); Abdul Ghaffar Khan was also known as "Frontier Gandhi"; British Indian soldiers in Peshawar refused to fire on non-violent protesters.
claims.quote: সংগঠনটির নাম ছিল খুদা ই-খিদমদগার। লাল রং-এর কুর্তা পরতেন বলে তাঁদের লালকুর্তা বাহিনীও বলা হতো। গান্ধি-অনুগামী হওয়ার সুবাদে আবদুল গফফর খান ‘সীমান্ত গান্ধি’ নামেও পরিচিত হন। পেশোয়ারে ব্রিটিশ সেনা বাহিনীর সিপাহিরা অহিংস আন্দোলনকারীর উপর গুলি চালাতে অস্বীকার করে।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in the Naga area the young Rani Gidalo joined the revolt against British rule.
claims.quote: নাগা অঞ্চলে তরুণী রানি গিদালো ব্রিটিশ শাসনের বিরুদ্ধে বিদ্রোহে শামিল হন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in the 1930s a peasant movement was organised in Sylhet and Mymensingh under Maulana Abdul Hamid Khan Bhasani.
claims.quote: ১৯৩০-এর দশকে মৌলানা আবদুল হামিদ খান ভাসানির নেতৃত্বে সিলেট, ময়মনসিংহ প্রভৃতি অঞ্চলে কৃষক আন্দোলন সংগঠিত হয়েছিল।

claims.claim: WBBSE: the British used the usual repression; the Congress was banned as a political organisation and nationalist newspapers put under severe restrictions.
claims.quote: আইন অমান্য আন্দোলনে ব্রিটিশ সরকার প্রচলিত দমননীতির সাহায্য নিয়েছিল। রাজনৈতিক সংগঠন হিসেবে কংগ্রেসকে নিষিদ্ধ ঘোষণা করা হয়। পাশাপাশি জাতীয়তাবাদী সংবাদপত্রগুলিকেও কঠোর বিধিনিষেধের আওতায় আনা হয়েছিল।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in 1930 the British called a meeting to discuss the Simon Commission report; the Congress boycotted it, so a second meeting was arranged.
claims.quote: তার পাশাপাশি ব্রিটিশ সরকার ১৯৩০ খ্রিস্টাব্দে একটি বৈঠক ডাকে। ঐ বৈঠকের উদ্দেশ্য ছিল সাইমন কমিশনের রিপোর্ট নিয়ে আলোচনা করা। কংগ্রেস ঐ বৈঠক বয়কট করে। ফলে দ্বিতীয়বার বৈঠকের উদ্যোগ নেওয়া হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: civil disobedience began again early in 1932; over a lakh went to jail in 1932-33; the second phase was not very successful; withdrawn unconditionally in May 1934.
claims.quote: ১৯৩২ খ্রিস্টাব্দের শুরু থেকে আবার আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন শুরু হয়। বিক্ষোভ মিছিলের পাশাপাশি বিদেশি কাপড় বর্জন করা ও ভূমিরাজস্ব কর না দেওয়ার উদ্যোগও নেওয়া হয়। ১৯৩২ থেকে ১৯৩৩ খ্রিস্টাব্দের মধ্যে লক্ষাধিক মানুষ আন্দোলনের জন্য জেলে যান। তবে দ্বিতীয় পর্যায়ের আইন অমান্য বিশেষ সফল হয়নি। ১৯৩৪ খ্রিস্টাব্দের মে মাসে আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন নিঃশর্তভাবে তুলে নেওয়া হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: urban educated middle-class participation was low, workers also joined less; peasants and businessmen joined in greater numbers.
claims.quote: পাশাপাশি শহুরে শিক্ষিত ও মধ্যবিত্ত মানুষের যোগদান আইন অমান্য আন্দোলনে কম ছিল। একইভাবে ১৯৩০ খ্রিস্টাব্দের আন্দোলনে শ্রমিকরাও কম যোগ দিয়েছিলেন। তবে কৃষক ও ব্যবসায়ীরা বেশি সংখ্যায় যুক্ত হয়েছিলেন আইন অমান্য আন্দোলনে।

claims.claim: WBBSE: the pact between Gandhi and Lord Irwin on 4 March 1931, also called the Delhi Pact: non-violent satyagrahi prisoners released, boycott of British goods not allowed, repressive laws withdrawn; Congress to withdraw civil disobedience and Gandhi to attend the second London conference.
claims.quote: ১৯৩১ খ্রিস্টাব্দের ৪ মার্চ গান্ধি ও লর্ড আরউইনের মধ্যে যে চুক্তি হয় তাকে দিল্লি চুক্তিও বলে। সেই চুক্তিতে ঠিক হয় অহিংস সত্যাগ্রহী বন্দিদের ব্রিটিশ সরকার ছেড়ে দেবে। ব্রিটিশ পণ্য বর্জন করা চলবে না। দমনমূলক আইনগুলি সরকার তুলে নেবে। এসবের বদলে কংগ্রেস আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন প্রত্যাহার করবে। পাশাপাশি লন্ডনে দ্বিতীয় বৈঠকে গান্ধি যোগ দেবেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: Gandhi was disappointed by the second Round Table Conference and civil disobedience began again.
claims.quote: কিন্তু দ্বিতীয় গোলটেবিল বৈঠকের আলোচনায় গান্ধি হতাশ হন। ফলে আবার আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন শুরু হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: on 18 April 1930 the Chittagong armoury was raided under Surya Sen's leadership.
claims.quote: অনুযায়ী সূর্য সেনের নেতৃত্বে ১৯৩০ খ্রিস্টাব্দের ১৮ এপ্রিল চট্টগ্রাম অস্ত্রাগার লুণ্ঠন করা হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in 1930 Muslim League president Iqbal, and later Cambridge student Choudhary Rahmat Ali, proposed a separate territory for Muslims comprising Punjab, NWFP, Baluchistan and Kashmir.
claims.quote: খ্রিস্টাব্দে মুসলিম লিগের সভাপতি মহম্মদ ইকবাল এবং পরে কেম্ব্রিজ বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের ছাত্র চৌধুরি রহমৎ আলি পঞ্জাব, উত্তর-পশ্চিম সীমান্ত প্রদেশ, বালুচিস্তান ও কাশ্মীর নিয়ে মুসলমানদের আলাদা ভূ-খণ্ড গঠন করার প্রস্তাব দেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: Rahmat Ali vaguely mentioned "Pakistan".
claims.quote: রহমৎ আলি অস্পষ্টভাবে ‘পাকিস্তান’-এর কথা উল্লেখ করেছিলেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: in 1932 British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald's announcement spoke of the Communal Award (সাম্প্রদায়িক বাঁটোয়ারা), reflecting divide and rule; some legislative seats were allotted to each minority.
claims.quote: ১৯৩২ খ্রিস্টাব্দে ব্রিটিশ প্রধানমন্ত্রী র‍্যামসে ম্যাকডোনাল্ড-এর ঘোষণায় সাম্প্রদায়িক বাঁটোয়ারার কথা বলা হয়। সেই ঘোষণায় ব্রিটিশ সরকারের বিভাজন ও শাসন নীতিই প্রতিফলিত হয়েছিল। ঐ ঘোষণা মোতাবেক প্রতিটি সংখ্যালঘু সম্প্রদায়ের জন্য বিধানমণ্ডলীতে কিছু আসন বরাদ্দ করা হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: election by separate communities was proposed; the Congress opposed such separate electorates because they would encourage communal feeling instead of nationalist unity.
claims.quote: সম্প্রদায়ের ভিত্তিতে নির্বাচন করার কথা ওঠে। কংগ্রেস এই ধরনের পৃথক নির্বাচকমণ্ডলীর বিরোধী ছিল। কারণ তার ফলে জাতীয়তাবাদী ঐক্যের বদলে সাম্প্রদায়িক ভাবনাকেই উৎসাহ দেওয়া হত।

claims.claim: WBBSE: during Civil Disobedience Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for dalits; Gandhi opposed; in 1932 separate electorates were granted to Scheduled Castes; Gandhi began a fast unto death; Ambedkar asked him to end it.
claims.quote: আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন চলাকালীন আম্বেদকর দাবি করেন দলিত সমাজের রাজনৈতিক অধিকার রক্ষার জন্য তাদের আলাদা নির্বাচনের অধিকার দিতে হবে। কিন্তু মহাত্মা গান্ধি আম্বেদকরের এই প্রস্তাবের বিরোধিতা করেন। ১৯৩২ খ্রিস্টাব্দে দলিত মানুষদের তফশিলি জাতি হিসাবে আলাদা নির্বাচনের অধিকার দেওয়া হয়। তার প্রতিবাদে গান্ধি আমরণ অনশন শুরু করেন। ফলে বাধ্য হয়ে আম্বেদকর গান্ধিকে অনশন তুলে নিতে অনুরোধ করেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: under the Poona Pact, instead of separate electorates, 151 seats were reserved for Scheduled Castes in joint electorates.
claims.quote: (পুনা চুক্তি) হয়। সেই চুক্তি অনুসারে দলিতদের আলাদা নির্বাচনের বদলে যৌথ নির্বাচনেই তফশিলি জাতির জন্য ১৫১টি আসন সংরক্ষণের ব্যবস্থা করা হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: under the 1935 Act provincial legislature elections were held in 1937; the Congress succeeded but the League did not do so well.
claims.quote: ভারত শাসন আইন (১৯৩৫ খ্রি.) মোতাবেক প্রাদেশিক বিধানমণ্ডলীর জন্য নির্বাচন অনুষ্ঠিত হয় ১৯৩৭ খ্রিস্টাব্দে। এই নির্বাচনে কংগ্রেস সাফল্য পেলেও, লিগ ততটা ভালো ফল করতে

claims.claim: WBBSE (as printed): in Punjab, Bengal, Assam, NWFP and Sind, the Muslim-majority provinces, a Congress ministry was formed.
claims.quote: মুসলমান জনসংখ্যা-প্রধান পঞ্জাব, বাংলা, আসাম, উত্তর-পশ্চিম সীমান্ত প্রদেশ ও সিন্ধ প্রভৃতি প্রদেশে কংগ্রেসি মন্ত্রীসভা তৈরি হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE: Fazlul Huq's Krishak Praja Party in Bengal and Sikandar Hayat Khan's Unionist Party in the Punjab did not strengthen the demand for a separate state; the KPP also fought the League for Muslim votes; until 1937 the League had little influence in most areas.
claims.quote: জাতির হিন্দু ও মুসলমান উভয় কৃষকদের স্বার্থের পক্ষেই সওয়াল করত। এমনকি মুসলিম ভোট নিয়ে লিগের সঙ্গে কৃষক প্রজা পার্টির লড়াইও চলেছিল। বস্তুত, ১৯৩৭ খ্রিস্টাব্দ পর্যন্ত কিছু শিক্ষিত মুসলমানদের বাইরে অধিকাংশ অঞ্চলেই লিগের বিশেষ প্রভাব ছিল না। বাংলায় ফজলুল হক-এর কৃষক প্রজা পার্টি বা পঞ্জাবে স্যর সিকন্দর হায়াৎ খান-এর ইউনিয়নিস্ট পার্টি আলাদা রাষ্ট্রের দাবিকে জোরদার করেনি।

claims.claim: WBBSE exercise: the leader of the Krishak Praja Party was A. K. Fazlul Huq.
claims.quote: কৃষক প্রজা পার্টির নেতা ছিলেন

claims.claim: WBBSE: Subhas Bose was nominated Congress president at Haripura 1938; bitterness with Gandhi and his followers grew; at Tripuri 1939 he defeated the Gandhi-nominated Pattabhi Sitaramayya and was elected president again, but later resigned and formed the Forward Bloc within the party.
claims.quote: ১৯৩৮ খ্রিস্টাব্দের হরিপুরায় সুভাষচন্দ্র বসু কংগ্রেসের সভাপতি মনোনীত হন। কিন্তু ক্রমে গান্ধি ও তাঁর অনুগামীদের সঙ্গে নবীন নেতৃত্বের তিক্ততা বাড়তে থাকে। ১৯৩৯ খ্রিস্টাব্দের ত্রিপুরি কংগ্রেসে গান্ধি-মনোনীত প্রার্থী পট্টভি সীতারামাইয়াকে হারিয়ে সুভাষচন্দ্র আবার সভাপতি নির্বাচিত হন। কিন্তু পরে পদ ত্যাগ করে দলের মধ্যেই সহমর্মীদের নিয়ে সুভাষচন্দ্র ফরওয়ার্ড ব্লক তৈরি করেন।

claims.claim: WBBSE: Sarat Chandra Bose was suspended for indiscipline and Subhas barred from contesting elected Congress posts for three years.
claims.quote: শরৎচন্দ্র বসুকে শৃঙ্খলাভঙ্গের অভিযোগে সাসপেন্ড করে। সুভাষকে কংগ্রেসের কোনো নির্বাচিত পদে লড়াই করার ক্ষেত্রে তিন-বছরের জন্য নিষিদ্ধ করা হয়।

claims.claim: WBBSE (Subhas section): the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn in 1933, after which Subhas sharply criticised Congress policy.
claims.quote: ১৯৩৩ খ্রিস্টাব্দে আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন তুলে নেওয়া হলে সুভাষচন্দ্র কংগ্রেসের নীতির তীব্র সমালোচনা করেন।

questions.q: ১৯২২ সালের ফেব্রুয়ারিতে কোন ঘটনার পর গান্ধি অসহযোগ আন্দোলন তুলে নেন?
questions.a: চৌরিচৌরায় থানায় আগুন দেওয়া ও পুলিশের মৃত্যু
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: ১৯২২ সালের ফেব্রুয়ারিতে চৌরিচৌরায় একদল কৃষক থানা পুড়িয়ে দিলে ২২ জন পুলিশ মারা যান, আর গান্ধি আন্দোলন তুলে নেন। সাইমন কমিশন, লাজপত রায়ের মৃত্যু ও ডান্ডি অভিযান সবই পরের (১৯২৭–৩০) ঘটনা।

questions.q: কংগ্রেসের ভেতরে স্বরাজ্য দল গঠন করেন কারা?
questions.a: চিত্তরঞ্জন দাশ ও মতিলাল নেহরু
w: বল্লভভাই প্যাটেল ও লালা লাজপত রায়
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: ক্লাস দশের এনসিইআরটি বই বলছে, সি. আর. দাশ ও মতিলাল নেহরু স্বরাজ্য দল গড়েন। জওহরলাল নেহরু ও সুভাষ বরং আরও জোরালো গণআন্দোলন চাইছিলেন; প্যাটেল বারদৌলির নেতা, লাজপত রায় সাইমন-বিরোধী আন্দোলনে আহত হন।

questions.q: সাইমন কমিশন বয়কটের মূল কারণ কী ছিল?
questions.a: কমিশনে একজনও ভারতীয় সদস্য ছিলেন না
w: কমিশন লবণ-কর বাড়ানোর জন্য গঠিত হয়েছিল
কমিশনের নেতৃত্বে ছিলেন ভাইসরয় লর্ড আরউইন
কমিশন কংগ্রেসকে বাদ দিয়ে শুধু মুসলিম লীগের সমর্থন পেয়েছিল
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: কমিশনের সবাই ব্রিটিশ ছিলেন, একজনও ভারতীয় ছিলেন না। কমিশনের নেতা ছিলেন স্যার জন সাইমন। বয়কটে কংগ্রেস ও মুসলিম লীগ-সহ সব দল যোগ দিয়েছিল, তাই লীগের সমর্থনের কথা ভুল।

questions.q: ১৯২৮ সালে লাহোরে সাইমন-বিরোধী মিছিলে পুলিশের লাঠিচার্জে আহত হয়ে কয়েক সপ্তাহের মধ্যে কোন নেতা মারা যান?
questions.a: লালা লাজপত রায়
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: লাজপত রায় আহত হয়ে দু-সপ্তাহ পরে মারা যান। দাশ মারা যান ১৯২৫ সালে, প্যাটেল বারদৌলির নেতা, আর নেহরু ১৯২৯ সালে লাহোর কংগ্রেসের সভাপতি হন।

questions.q: ১৯২৯ সালের লাহোর অধিবেশনে কংগ্রেস কোন দাবিকে আনুষ্ঠানিকভাবে লক্ষ্য বলে ঘোষণা করে?
questions.a: পূর্ণ স্বরাজ (সম্পূর্ণ স্বাধীনতা)
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: লাহোরে জওহরলাল নেহরুর সভাপতিত্বে কংগ্রেস পূর্ণ স্বরাজের দাবি ঘোষণা করে। ডোমিনিয়ন স্ট্যাটাস ছিল নেহরু রিপোর্টের (১৯২৮) দাবি।

questions.q: কংগ্রেসের ঘোষণা অনুযায়ী স্বাধীনতা দিবস কোন দিন পালিত হয়েছিল?
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: লাহোর কংগ্রেসের ঘোষণা মেনে ২৬ জানুয়ারি ১৯৩০ সারা দেশে স্বাধীনতা দিবস পালিত হয়। ১২ মার্চ ডান্ডি অভিযানের যাত্রা, ৬ এপ্রিল ডান্ডিতে আইন ভঙ্গ, ৫ মার্চ ১৯৩১ গান্ধি–আরউইন চুক্তি।

questions.q: লবণ অভিযানে গান্ধি কোন স্থান থেকে যাত্রা শুরু করেন?
questions.a: সবরমতী আশ্রম
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: গান্ধি সবরমতী আশ্রম থেকে হেঁটে গুজরাটের উপকূলের ডান্ডিতে যান। লাহোর কংগ্রেসের স্থান, পেশোয়ারে কিসসা খোয়ানির গুলিচালনা, চৌরিচৌরায় ১৯২২-এর ঘটনা।

questions.q: ডান্ডিতে লবণ আইন ভাঙার মধ্য দিয়ে কোন আন্দোলন শুরু হয়?
questions.a: আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: ১৯৩০ সালের ৬ এপ্রিল ডান্ডিতে লবণ আইন ভাঙার পর আইন অমান্য আন্দোলন শুরু হয়। অসহযোগ আন্দোলন (১৯২০-২২) ও বারদৌলি আগের, সাইমন-বিরোধী আন্দোলন অন্য ধরনের।

questions.q: গান্ধি–আরউইন চুক্তি কোন বছর সই হয়?
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: চুক্তি হয় ১৯৩১ সালের মার্চে (ক্লাস ১০: ৫ মার্চ; WBBSE: ৪ মার্চ)। ১৯২৯-এ আরউইনের অস্পষ্ট প্রস্তাব, ১৯৩০-এ ডান্ডি অভিযান, ১৯৩২-এ পুনা চুক্তি।

questions.q: পুনা চুক্তি কোন বছর হয়?
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: পুনা চুক্তি হয় ১৯৩২ সালের সেপ্টেম্বরে। ১৯৩০ ডান্ডি, ১৯৩১ গান্ধি–আরউইন চুক্তি, ১৯৩৪ আইন অমান্য প্রত্যাহার।

questions.q: ক্লাস দশের এনসিইআরটি বই অনুযায়ী গান্ধি ১৯২২ সালে অসহযোগ আন্দোলন প্রত্যাহার করেন কেন?
questions.a: আন্দোলন বহু জায়গায় হিংসার দিকে যাচ্ছিল এবং সত্যাগ্রহীদের আগে প্রশিক্ষণ দরকার ছিল
w: সরকার কংগ্রেসের সব দাবি মেনে নিয়েছিল
কংগ্রেসের সব নেতা আন্দোলন বন্ধ করতে চেয়েছিলেন
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: গান্ধির যুক্তি ছিল হিংসার দিকে ঝোঁক ও প্রশিক্ষণের অভাব। কংগ্রেসের অনেক নেতা (মতিলাল ও জওহরলাল নেহরু, দাশ, বসু) এই সিদ্ধান্তে অসন্তুষ্ট ছিলেন, তাই "সব নেতা চেয়েছিলেন" ভুল।

questions.q: স্বরাজ্য দলের কৌশল কী ছিল?
questions.a: নির্বাচনে লড়ে কাউন্সিলে ঢুকে ভেতর থেকে ব্রিটিশ নীতির বিরোধিতা করা
w: কাউন্সিল সম্পূর্ণ বয়কট করে গ্রামে চরকা প্রচার করা
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: দাশ ও মতিলাল নেহরু চেয়েছিলেন কাউন্সিলে ঢুকে নীতি প্রভাবিত করতে ও দেখাতে যে কাউন্সিল গণতান্ত্রিক নয়। গ্রামে গঠনমূলক কাজ ছিল গান্ধিপন্থীদের পথ।

questions.q: ১৯২৪ সালের ফেব্রুয়ারিতে জেল থেকে ছাড়া পেয়ে গান্ধি কোন কাজে বিশেষ মন দেন?
questions.a: খাদি প্রচার ও অস্পৃশ্যতা-দূরীকরণের মতো সমাজ-সংস্কারে
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: এনসিইআরটি বলছে, গান্ধি খাদির প্রচার ও সমাজ-সংস্কারে মন দেন; সাইমন কমিশন ও গোলটেবিল বৈঠক অনেক পরের ঘটনা, আর কাউন্সিলে ঢোকার পথ ছিল স্বরাজ্য দলের।

questions.q: সাইমন কমিশনের কাজ কী ছিল?
questions.a: ভারতের সাংবিধানিক ব্যবস্থা কেমন চলছে দেখে পরিবর্তনের সুপারিশ করা
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: কমিশন ভারতের সাংবিধানিক ব্যবস্থার কাজকর্ম খতিয়ে দেখে পরিবর্তন সুপারিশ করার জন্য গঠিত হয়েছিল।

questions.q: সাইমন-বিরোধী সর্বভারতীয় আন্দোলনে গান্ধির ভূমিকা কী ছিল?
questions.a: নিজে অংশ নেননি, কিন্তু আশীর্বাদ জানিয়েছিলেন
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: ক্লাস বারোর বই জানায়, ১৯২৮ সালে গান্ধি এই আন্দোলনে নিজে অংশ নেননি, তবে আশীর্বাদ দিয়েছিলেন; বারদৌলির কৃষক সত্যাগ্রহের ক্ষেত্রেও তাই।

questions.q: ১৯২৯ সালের ৮ এপ্রিল কেন্দ্রীয় আইনসভায় বোমা ছোড়ায় ভগৎ সিংয়ের সঙ্গী কে ছিলেন?
questions.a: বি. কে. দত্ত
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: এনসিইআরটি-র মতে ভগৎ সিং ও বি. কে. দত্ত বোমা ছোড়েন, উদ্দেশ্য ছিল "বধিরকে শোনানো"। সুখদেব ও রাজগুরু ভগৎ সিংয়ের সঙ্গে ১৯৩১-এর ফাঁসির সঙ্গী; ১৯২৮-এর সন্ডার্স হত্যায় ছিলেন ভগৎ সিং, আজাদ ও রাজগুরু।

questions.q: ১৯২৮ সালের নেহরু রিপোর্টে ভারতের জন্য কোন মর্যাদা চাওয়া হয়েছিল?
questions.a: ডোমিনিয়ন স্ট্যাটাস
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: মতিলাল নেহরুর সভাপতিত্বে লেখা রিপোর্ট ডোমিনিয়ন স্ট্যাটাস চেয়েছিল, যেখানে ব্রিটিশ সম্রাট বা সম্রাজ্ঞী রাষ্ট্রপ্রধান থেকে যান; পূর্ণ স্বাধীনতার দাবি এল লাহোরে।

questions.q: ১৯২৭-২৮ সালে জিন্নাহ কোন শর্তে পৃথক নির্বাচকমণ্ডলীর দাবি ছাড়তে রাজি ছিলেন?
questions.a: কেন্দ্রীয় আইনসভায় সংরক্ষিত আসন এবং বাংলা ও পাঞ্জাবে জনসংখ্যা-অনুপাতে প্রতিনিধিত্ব পেলে
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: ক্লাস দশের বই জিন্নাহর এই শর্ত দুটি জানায়। উত্তর-পশ্চিমে আলাদা অঞ্চলের প্রস্তাব এসেছিল ১৯৩০ সালে ইকবালের কাছ থেকে।

questions.q: ১৯২৮ সালের সর্বদলীয় সম্মেলনে সমঝোতার সব আশা কার তীব্র বিরোধিতায় শেষ হয়?
questions.a: এম. আর. জয়াকর (হিন্দু মহাসভা)
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: এনসিইআরটি-র মতে হিন্দু মহাসভার এম. আর. জয়াকর আপসের চেষ্টার তীব্র বিরোধিতা করায় আশা শেষ হয়। জিন্নাহ তো আপসের প্রস্তাব দিয়েছিলেন।

questions.q: লবণকে কেন প্রতিবাদের প্রতীক করা হয়েছিল?
questions.a: ধনী-গরিব সবার কাছে লবণ অপরিহার্য, আর তাতে সরকারের একচেটিয়া ও চড়া কর ছিল
w: লবণ কেবল গুজরাটের কৃষকদের প্রয়োজনীয় ছিল
লবণ-কর শুধু ব্রিটিশ বণিকদের ওপর বসত
লবণ আইন কেবল শিল্পপতিদের ক্ষতি করত
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: লবণ প্রতিটি ঘরে লাগে, অথচ ঘরের জন্যও বানানো নিষিদ্ধ ছিল; তাই লবণের ক্ষোভে ধনী-গরিবের ভেদ ছিল না। বাকি তিনটি বক্তব্য পাঠ্যবইয়ের বিরোধী।

questions.q: ডান্ডি অভিযানে গান্ধির সঙ্গে কতজন বিশ্বস্ত স্বেচ্ছাসেবক ছিলেন?
questions.a: ৭৮ জন
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: ক্লাস দশের বই বলছে ৭৮ জন। ১১ হল গান্ধির চিঠির দাবির সংখ্যা, ২৪০ হল মাইলে দূরত্ব।

questions.q: পাটিদার ও জাঠ ধনী কৃষকরা আইন অমান্যে উৎসাহী হয়েছিলেন কেন?
questions.a: মন্দায় বাণিজ্যিক ফসলের দাম পড়ে যাওয়ায় রাজস্ব মেটানো কঠিন হয়েছিল
w: তাঁরা জমিদারকে দেওয়া বকেয়া খাজনা মকুব চাইছিলেন
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: ধনী কৃষকরা বাণিজ্যিক ফসল ফলাতেন, তাই মন্দায় সবচেয়ে বেশি ক্ষতি হয়; তাঁদের কাছে স্বরাজের লড়াই ছিল চড়া রাজস্বের বিরুদ্ধে। বকেয়া খাজনা মকুব চেয়েছিলেন গরিব ভাগচাষিরা।

questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: সরোজিনী নাইডু ১৯২৫ সালে কংগ্রেসের প্রথম ভারতীয় মহিলা সভাপতি হন এবং ডান্ডি অভিযানের গুরুত্বপূর্ণ নেত্রী ছিলেন। কমলাদেবী ছিলেন সমাজতান্ত্রিক কর্মী; বীণা দাস ও সুনীতি চৌধুরী বাংলার বিপ্লবী ছাত্রী।

questions.a: হিংসায় জড়িত নয় এমন রাজনৈতিক বন্দিদের মুক্তি ও সীমিত পরিমাণে লবণ উৎপাদনের অনুমতি
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: চুক্তিতে বন্দিমুক্তি ও সীমিত লবণ-তৈরি মিলল; বিনিময়ে কংগ্রেস আইন অমান্য স্থগিত করল। স্বাধীনতার প্রতিশ্রুতি মেলেনি, তাই সমালোচনা হয়। কংগ্রেস বেআইনি হয় চুক্তির পর নতুন দমনের সময়।

questions.a: পৃথক নির্বাচকমণ্ডলীর বদলে ডিপ্রেসড ক্লাসেস-এর সংরক্ষিত আসন বাড়ল, যার প্রার্থী সাধারণ নির্বাচকমণ্ডলীর ভোটে নির্বাচিত

দলিতদের জন্য কোনো সংরক্ষিত আসন থাকল না
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: গান্ধির অনশনের পর আম্বেদকর তাঁর অবস্থান মেনে নেন; পৃথক নির্বাচকমণ্ডলী বাদ গেল, কিন্তু সংরক্ষিত আসন বাড়ল।

questions.q: ১৯৩৫ সালের ভারত শাসন আইন প্রদেশগুলিকে কী দিল?
questions.a: প্রাদেশিক স্বায়ত্তশাসন ও নির্বাচিত প্রাদেশিক সরকার
questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: আইনটি প্রাদেশিক স্বায়ত্তশাসন দেয়। কিন্তু ভোটার ছিল প্রাপ্তবয়স্কদের ১০–১৫%, আর প্রতিরক্ষা ও বৈদেশিক নীতি ব্রিটিশের হাতেই ছিল।

questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: আরউইন ১৯২৯-এর অক্টোবরে অনির্দিষ্ট ভবিষ্যতের জন্য ডোমিনিয়নের অস্পষ্ট প্রস্তাব দেন, কংগ্রেস সন্তুষ্ট হয়নি। বাকি তিনটি ঘটনা ১৯৩১, ১৯৩২ ও ১৯৩৫-এর, অর্থাৎ লাহোরের পরে।

questions.q: দ্বিতীয় গোলটেবিল বৈঠকে "কংগ্রেস গোটা ভারতের প্রতিনিধি" গান্ধির এই দাবিকে কারা চ্যালেঞ্জ করেন?

questions.q: দ্বিতীয় গোলটেবিল বৈঠকের পর ভারতে ফিরে গান্ধি কী দেখলেন?
questions.a: সরকার নতুন করে দমন শুরু করেছে: গফফর খান ও নেহরু জেলে, কংগ্রেস বেআইনি ঘোষিত

questions.q: ১৯৩০ সালে মুসলিম লীগের সভাপতি হিসেবে ইকবাল কী প্রস্তাব রেখেছিলেন (ক্লাস আটের *Exploring Society* অনুসারে)?
questions.a: বৃহত্তর ভারতীয় যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের ভেতরে উত্তর-পশ্চিম ভারতে মুসলমানদের জন্য একটি পৃথক অঞ্চল

questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: বইটি স্পষ্ট বলছে, এটি তখনও "পাকিস্তান"-এর সুনির্দিষ্ট ধারণা নয়; শব্দটি কয়েক বছর পরে এসেছে। আর মুসলমানরা সাধারণভাবে আইন অমান্য থেকে দূরে ছিলেন।

questions.q: ১৯৩৫ সালের আইন সম্পর্কে কোন বক্তব্যটি সঠিক?
questions.a: ব্রিটিশ-নিযুক্ত গভর্নর প্রদেশের শাসন নিজের হাতে নিতে পারতেন এবং ভোটার ছিল প্রাপ্তবয়স্কদের ১০–১৫%

questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: গভর্নর নিয়ন্ত্রণ ও সীমিত ভোটাধিকার দুটিই বইয়ে আছে। আইনটি ঔপনিবেশিক সরকারই প্রণয়ন করেছিল; বৈদেশিক নীতি ও প্রতিরক্ষা ব্রিটিশের হাতে ছিল।

questions.a: মুসলমানরা সংখ্যালঘু, কোনো গণতান্ত্রিক কাঠামোয় তাদের সবসময় দ্বিতীয় সারিতে থাকতে হবে

questions.a: ছবিতে গান্ধি ও সুভাষ হাসিমুখে আলাপরত হলেও তখন নানা বিষয়ে তাঁদের মতবিরোধ ছিল, এবং পরের বছর সুভাষ কংগ্রেস-সভাপতির পদ ছাড়েন

questions.e: ব্যাখ্যা: বইয়ের বার্তা: ছবি দেখে মনোভাব সবসময় বোঝা যায় না; পদত্যাগ ছিল "পরের বছর", আর ছবিতে গান্ধি ও সুভাষ। নতুন দলের কথা এই সূত্রে নেই।
